<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par116 />with it in the construct state, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=18|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=9|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=לָבוּשׁ בַּדִּים|translate=clothed in linen}}, cf. verse 3 {{GHGheb|text=הַלָּבֻשׁ הַבַּדִּים}}; (even with a suffix {{GHGheb|text=קָרוּעַ כֻּתָּנְתּוֹ|translate=rent as regards his coat}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=15|verse=32}}; with the participle following {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=1|verse=7}}); but {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=9|verse=11}} {{GHGheb|text=לְבוּשׁ הַבַּדִּים|translate=the one clothed with linen}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=13|verse=31}} {{GHGheb|text=קְרֻעֵי בְגָדִים|translate=rent in respect of clothes}}, equivalent to ''with their clothes rent'' (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=41|verse=5}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=24|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=25|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=3|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=33|verse=24|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jo|chapter=1|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=32|verse=1}} ({{GHGheb|text=נְשׂוּי־פֶּ֫שַׁע|translate=forgiven in respect of transgression}}, {{GHGheb|text=כְּסוּי חֲטָאָה|translate=covered in respect of sin}}); with a suffix to the noun, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=14|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=נְלוֹז דְּרָכָיו|translate=he that is perverse in his ways}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|116|l}}
Rem. The passive participle occurs in the construct state before a genitive of the ''cause'', e.g. in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=שְׂרֻפוֹת אֵשׁ|translate=burnt with fire}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=28|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=24}}; before a genitive denoting the ''author'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=31}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּרוּךְ יְהֹוָה|translate=blessed of the Lord}} (but {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=115|verse=15}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּרוּכִים לַיהוָֹה}}, see {{GHGpar|121|f}}); cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=53|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=22|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=14|verse=1}} (15:14, 25:4); hence also with noun-suffixes (which are accordingly genitive) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=9|verse=18}} {{GHGheb|text=קְרֻאֶ֫יהָ|translate=her invited ones}}, i.e. those invited by her; cf. 7:26, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=37|verse=22}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|116|m}}
'''5.''' The use of the participle as predicate is very frequent in noun-clauses (which, according to {{GHGpar|140|e}}, describe established facts and states), in which the period of time intended by the description must again (see above, d) be inferred from the context. Thus:

{{GHGmargin-letter|116|n}}
(''a'') As ''present'', in speaking of truths which hold good at all times, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=1|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=דּוֹר הֹלֵךְ וְדוֹר בָּא}} ''one generation goeth, and another generation cometh; and the earth abideth'' ({{GHGheb|text=עֹמָ֫דֶת}}) ''for ever''; cf. verse 7; also to represent incidental (continuous) occurrences which are just happening, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=3|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=16|verse=8|hidebook=1}} (''I am fleeing''); 32:12, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=9|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=16|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=23|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=7|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=1|verse=7}}; when the subject is introduced by the emphatic demonstrative {{GHGheb|text=הִנֵּה|translate=behold!}} ({{GHGpar|100|o}} and {{GHGpar|105|b}}), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=16|verse=11}} {{GHGheb|text=הִנָּךְ הָרָה|translate=behold, thou art with child}}, &c.; 27:42; frequently also in circumstantial clauses (connected by {{GHGterm|Wāw}}), cf. {{GHGpar|141|e}}, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=15|verse=2}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|116|o}}
(''b'') To represent ''past'' actions or states, sometimes in independent noun-clauses, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=20|verse=18}} {{GHGheb|text=וְכָל־הָעָם רֹאִים אֶת־הַקּוֹלֹת|translate=and all the people saw the thunderings}}, &c.; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=1|verse=5}}; in negative statements, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=39|verse=23}}<sup> ''a''</sup>; sometimes in relativeclauses, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=39|verse=23}}<sup> ''b''</sup>, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=3|verse=2}} (cf. also the frequent combination of the participle with the article as the equivalent of a relative clause, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=הָֽאֹמֵר|translate=which saidst}}; 12:7, 16:13, 35:1, 3, 36:35, 48:16, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=15|verse=31}}, &c.); sometimes again (see n) in ''circumstantial'' clauses, especially those representing actions or states which occurred simultaneously with other past actions, &c., e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=1}} ''and the two angels came to Sodom'' {{GHGheb|text=וְלוֹט ישֵׁב|translate=and}} (i.e. ''while'') ''Lot sat'', &c.; 18:1, 8, 16, 22, 25:26, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=13|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=22|verse=9}}; also with the subject introduced by {{GHGheb|text=הִנֵּה}} 37:7, 41:17. (On {{GHGheb|text=הֹלֵךְ}} with a following adjective or participle to express an action constantly or occasionally recurring, cf. {{GHGpar|113|u}}.)

{{GHGmargin-letter|116|p}}
(''c'') To announce ''future'' actions or events, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=2|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=4|verse=16}} ''at this season when the time cometh round'', {{GHGheb|text=אַתְּ חֹבֶ֫קֶת בֵּן|translate=thou shalt embrace a son}}; so after a specification of time, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=7|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=15|verse=14|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=17|verse=19|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=13|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hag|chapter=2|verse=6}} (but in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=23|verse=15}}, where, after {{GHGheb|text=וְהָיָה}} we should rather expect a perfect consecutive, it is better to explain<section end=par116 /><noinclude>
